entries.what_happened: The family has one manuscript, 'Fujita's freeness conjecture' (OpenAI, dated September 23, 2026). Its main theorem: for X a smooth connected projective variety over ℂ of dimension n ≥ 1 and L an ample line bundle on X, Kₓ + (n+1)L is generated by its global sections. A corollary (cor:all-powers) deduces that Kₓ + mL is globally generated for every integer m ≥ n+1, by applying the main theorem to X × ℙʳ with r = m−n−1 and the ample bundle L ⊠ O(1); the adjoint bundle there is (Kₓ + mL) ⊠ O(n), and its restriction to X × {z} is Kₓ + mL. The text gives ℙⁿ with L = O(1) as the sharpness example: Kₓ + (n+1)L is trivial while Kₓ + nL has no nonzero sections. The proof is by contradiction at a point x. (i) An 'ordinary-order alternative' shows that failure of generation at x forces a strict asymptotic inequality for the mean ordinary order of bases of H⁰(X, mL). (ii) The proof minimizes an exponential functional over bases of H⁰(X, mL) and weighted monomial valuations whose centers contain x, for a fixed t < n+1. It shows the minimum is attained and has bounded discrepancy. (iii) A tangential variation of a minimizer, a uniform lower estimate on restriction spaces, and a discrete Brunn–Minkowski inequality show that minimizers have center exactly {x} in arbitrarily large degrees. (iv) A rational supporting profile is used to build an effective SNC boundary and a reduced divisor S over x on which the boundary coefficient equals the log discrepancy and is strictly smaller on neighbouring components. (v) Kawamata–Viehweg vanishing, in Fujino's logarithmic form, lifts a nonzero value from S, and descent gives a section of Kₓ + (n+1)L that is nonzero at x. This contradicts the assumed failure.
entries.delivers: For the freeness (global generation) part of the list's problem: for every smooth complex projective variety X of dimension n and every ample L on X, Kₓ + mL is globally generated for every m ≥ n+1. The threshold n+1 is the sharp one, per the sharpness example. Restrictions: the setting is smooth projective varieties over ℂ, not compact complex manifolds with a positive holomorphic bundle; L must be ample; the theorem assumes connectedness, which the text says only fixes notation (applies componentwise). The manuscript states its result as a proof of Fujita's freeness conjecture. Its freeness statement matches part (a) of the list's problem, at threshold m ≥ n+1. The manuscript does not claim the whole problem as the list words it: the list's problem also covers very ampleness (part (b)), which the Introduction says is not asserted. The list's compact-complex-manifold formulation is not addressed in the manuscript. The research pass's reduction (a positive holomorphic bundle on a compact complex manifold makes it projective via Kodaira's embedding theorem, with L ample) would bring it into scope, but the manuscript does not state this reduction.
entries.remains: Part (b) of the problem: very ampleness of Kₓ + mL for m ≥ n+2, using the research pass's threshold. The Introduction explicitly says the manuscript does not assert separation of points or tangent directions, or the very-ampleness part of Fujita's conjecture. The compact-complex-manifold formulation is not treated directly in the text. Nothing is claimed for m ≤ n, and the sharpness example shows that m = n cannot work in general.
entries.direction: proves the freeness conjecture (global generation) at the sharp threshold m ≥ n+1; the very-ampleness part is not addressed
entries.doubts: (1) Several steps are given in condensed form. The constructibility half of the closed-threshold-locus lemma (lem:lct-family) is argued by saying it parallels the proof of Demailly–Kollár, with a stratification sketched in a few sentences. The multiplicity bound in lem:min-initials is justified in two sentences via a general curve. The claim that every fixed ball meets j⁻¹Hⱼ along the subsequence, which the ordinary-order alternative relies on, is argued in one paragraph without explicit constants. The compactness step in the existence of minimizers asserts that section orders are linear in the weights on the fixed model. (2) The final lift is described as following the discrepancy-and-vanishing strategy of Fujita 1993, §1(1.6), but the text writes out the lift itself and does not separately verify the adaptation. (3) The claim is much stronger than the bounds the Introduction itself cites. The sharpest general bounds it lists are of order n: Han, m ≥ ⌈C₀n⌉ with C₀ ≈ 1.776, and Ghidelli–Lacini, m ≥ n(log log n + 2.34) for n ≥ 2. The Introduction says the sharp bound is known for curves, for surfaces (Reider), and for dimensions three to five (Ein–Lazarsfeld, Kawamata, Ye–Zhu). The all-dimension claim is stated without hedging. (4) The Introduction records that a 2024 preprint by Chan, claiming a stronger intersection-number form, was withdrawn because a local extension argument did not guarantee the required vanishing order. The manuscript's final step is also a vanishing-based extension from a divisor over x. The text does not say explicitly how that failure is avoided beyond the isolation lemma. (5) The abstract does not state the connectedness hypothesis that the main theorem includes. The text says this only fixes notation, which I take at its word.
